summary: Iteration 43 follow-up: both fixes verified end-to-end. Fix 1 — POST /api/admin/sentry/test-error now correctly returns {ok:false, note:'...SENTRY_DSN env var missing...'} when DSN unset (early-return added before capture_exception). Fix 2 — POST /api/gdpr/delete-account no longer scrubs email/name/phone/photo; only sets deleted_at/purge_at/deletion_reason, so cancel is a clean $unset restoring full account state, and the seed client@crewfit.com survives the full delete/cancel cycle. Full cycle verified with a fresh signup user (signup → delete → /auth/me shows original PII + deleted_at → cancel → /auth/me clean → login with original creds works → cleanup). Regressions green: 18/18 test_launch_hardening.py + 12/12 test_beta_readiness.py + 10/10 new test_iter43_followup.py = 40/40. One stale assertion in test_launch_hardening.py::TestGDPR::test_delete_and_cancel_flow was updated (it asserted the OLD scrubbed 'deleted+' email pattern; now locates the pending row by deletion_reason instead) — test-only change consistent with the new correct behavior. Seed client account cleaned up (had a lingering pending delete from prior iter-43 run; cancelled via API, PII fully intact, login OK). Scope was backend-only per review request; frontend NOT tested.
critical_code_review_comments: feature_gdpr.py:97-127 — Deferred-scrub design is now sound. PII is preserved during the 30-day grace window and only removed at final purge time when the whole user row is deleted anyway. Consistent, reversible, and safe for test suites.

feature_beta_readiness.py:153-167 — Explicit env-var guard before capture_exception is correct: sentry_sdk.capture_exception is a silent no-op when no client is initialised, so guarding with `if not os.environ.get('SENTRY_DSN')` gives callers a truthful response body.

Minor housekeeping (non-blocking): test_iter43_followup.py uses a class-scoped fixture defined as an instance method (pytest deprecation warning). Consider @classmethod or module-level fixture. Does not affect correctness.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_launch_hardening.py (updated TestGDPR.test_delete_and_cancel_flow assertion — now locates pending row by deletion_reason instead of the obsolete `deleted+` scrubbed-email pattern)

success_rate.frontend: not tested (backend-only scope per review request)

seed_data_creation: One ephemeral signup user per followup run (gdpr-verify+<ts>-<rand>@test.com) is marked for deletion at the end and will hard-purge after the 30-day grace via the daily cron. Cancelled a stale pending-delete on client@crewfit.com left over from the previous iter-43 launch-hardening run — email/name/all profile fields fully preserved (verified via /api/auth/me). No lingering scrubbed rows.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Both iter-43 issues are fully resolved. Sentry test-error correctly reports missing DSN. GDPR delete/cancel cycle is non-destructive — safe to run test_launch_hardening.TestGDPR.test_delete_and_cancel_flow repeatedly against the seeded client@crewfit.com account. The updated assertion in test_launch_hardening.py identifies the pending row by deletion_reason='TEST_iteration_42', which is unique to that test and won't collide with other pending rows. If future test agents see leftover pending rows in /api/admin/gdpr/pending (e.g. from aborted runs), they can be safely cancelled via POST /api/gdpr/delete-account/cancel while authenticated as the affected user.
rca_of_issue: No new bugs surfaced. The two prior-iteration issues are resolved: (1) Sentry endpoint's silent-noop path fixed by early-return when SENTRY_DSN is absent — verified in production preview where DSN is unset. (2) Destructive PII scrub on delete-account replaced with deferred-scrub — only deleted_at/purge_at/deletion_reason are set on the user document during the 30-day grace period, so cancel is a lossless operation via $unset. End-to-end cycle test (signup→delete→me→cancel→me→login→cleanup) all green on 10/10 assertions.
